newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends higher in day of mixed, indecisive trade.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends higher in day of mixed, indecisive trade.

text.p: U.S. stocks ended mixed on Monday in a day of indecisive trading that had investors awaiting news on IBM's quarterly profits and congressional testimony from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan.
The Dow industrials spent the session shifting between positive and negative ground. The blue-chip gauge ended up 16 points at 7907, stabilizing after Friday's 130-point drop.
"I think people are kind of resting before the next wave," said James Volk, director of equity trading at Jensen Securities.
But further profit taking, particularly in high technology stocks, clipped broader indexes.
Declining issues outnumbered gainers on the New York Stock Exchange by a 19-to-nine ratio.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite slipped 12 points to 1536. It was led lower by shares of Microsoft Corp, which shed 4-9/16 to 135-15/16 in the second day of selling following the company's quarterly profit report last week.
But many investors appeared to hold off bets awaiting the earnings report from International Business Machines Corp, issued shortly after the market's close.
IBM reported reported second quarter earnings of $1.46 a share, up from $1.26 a year ago, adjusted for a stock split. It beat Wall Street's consensus forecast of $1.42.
Market players said that IBM's results could help sooth some of the overall market's recent nervousness.
"I don't think there's any shock here either way," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manger at Unity Management. "But the fact is that they beat the number."
On Tuesday, Wall Street will be on edge for any comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan on the direction of the economy, interest rates or the stock market itself.
Greenspan will deliver his mandatory semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before Congress on Tuesday beginning at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT and Wednesday at 1000 EDT/1800 GMT.
Analysts said they expect Greenspan to say the central bank needs to be wary of inflation, despite recent economic data showing muted price rises.
"The market will likely be on hold on the downside until we get through Greenspan," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
Given the sharp gains in stock prices so far this year, unexpected news coming from Greenspan, or elsewhere, could trigger a fresh wave of selling, analysts said.
"I think we're vulnerable to a correction, so any kind of bad news is probably going to be very negative for the market," said John Church, chief investment officer at Glenmede Trust Co.
First Union Corp said it will acquire Signet Banking Corp for about $3.2 billion in stock. Signet jumped 13-8/16 to 50-3/16 while First Union fell three to 94-7/16.
The day saw quarterly earnings reports from several members of the Dow industrials.

AT&T Corp ended off 1/8 to 34-1/4. The telecommunications giant reported a 36 percent decline in profits for the second quarter but results were slightly above Wall Street analysts' reduced expectations.

Exxon Corp beat even the most optimistic forecasts with its second quarter earnings, and its shares rose 14/16 to 61-5/16. Boeing Co fell 1-11/16 to 54-3/8 after reporting second quarter earnings that were below Wall Street expectations.

Elsewhere, Kimberly-Clark Corp fell 4-5/16 to 47-5/16 after reporting slightly lower second quarter earnings, saying its results were hurt by the combination of Scott Paper Co's operations, which it acquired in 1995.

3Dfx Interactive Inc. sank 4-1/8 to 12 after the computer chip maker said Sega Enterprises Ltd, a key customer, has not yet decided whether it will use a 3Dfx chip in its next-generation video game machine.
The S&P 500 fell 2.36 points to 912.94.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 11.76 points to 1536.23.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
